# Scope, limitations, and conclusion

The extreme sparse public-relay result is one Gemma 3 270M feature set, one
dictionary, and one grammatical mediator. S1 is attribution-selected and
amplified \(5\times\), so we identify the route of this causal handle rather
than a unique natural ontology. The private experiments use full residual
directions and establish causal capacity, not a sparse natural carrier. Their
effects exist at both scales but do not support monotone scaling.

The synonym double dissociation is the strongest routing result, but it is a
controlled route-recruitment assay at Gemma 3 1B. Donor prompts explicitly name
the source and target words; the neutral evaluated prompt does not. The six
between- and eight within-class sets use different semantic families, and no
within-`an` set passed screening. Thus the result does not establish spontaneous
carrier selection, a sparse routing controller, or universality across models
and mediators. A matched-semantic-triad extension and replication in another
model family are the highest-value next tests. The released `is/are` arithmetic
task did not pass local target efficacy and cannot adjudicate mediator capacity.

Greedy claims are supplemented by exact conditional `a/an` mixtures, not
unrestricted sampling over all tokens. The binary estimand is valid only when
article support is retained. The gain identity is algebraic. At 270M its
predictive validation identifies the high-gain regime, but ranking among small
effects is weak and crossed feature--prompt uncertainty is wide; transfer is
also weak at 1B. `a/an` offers limited variation in branch leverage. All
intervals reflect the finite prompt, feature, or semantic-family sets, not a
population of tasks.

Within those bounds, the conclusion is clear. Autoregressive output is part of
the circuit. Future-relevant causal influence can persist in private context or
be projected into a generated symbol and returned through feedback. Which
distinctions the symbol expresses constrains the route available to them, and
decoder susceptibility plus continuation leverage determine the gain of the
public loop. Mechanistic interpretation should therefore identify not only what
an intervention changes, but where that change travels.

**Ethics.** This public-model study uses synthetic prompts and no human or
personal data. AI-agent assistance is declared in the NeurIPS checklist.
